cases.title: Nominal geometry
cases.description: Two calibrated synthetic views observe the same moving person.
cases.risk: Synthetic agreement does not verify a physical rig.

cases.title: Missing hip
cases.description: The secondary view has no left-hip measurement; other joints can remain available.
cases.risk: A root requires both accepted hips. Missing coordinates stay unavailable.

cases.title: Uncertain identity
cases.description: The cross-view association is not confirmed.
cases.risk: Reconstruction is suspended rather than guessing a person's identity.

cases.title: Exposure skew
cases.description: The two synthetic exposures are 16 ms apart.
cases.risk: Fast motion can amplify depth error; simultaneous host reads do not prove simultaneous exposures.

cases.title: Exposure uncertainty
cases.description: Each synthetic source declares 10 ms of timing uncertainty.
cases.risk: An uncertain exposure cannot be certified by a manual synchronization checklist.

cases.title: Weak geometry
cases.description: The illustrative baseline is only 6 cm.
cases.risk: Nearly parallel rays cannot support useful depth, even with small image residuals.

cases.title: Calibration revision changed
cases.description: The secondary observation names a different calibration revision.
cases.risk: Moving a camera or changing image geometry invalidates the previous calibration.

cases.title: Hidden scale bias
cases.description: The calibration baseline is 5% larger than the independent synthetic reference.
cases.risk: Wrong metric scale can pass geometric gates. Compare the estimate with independent reference truth.

cases.title: Stale source pair
cases.description: These recorded sources were evaluated 100 ms after their observation time.
cases.risk: An old position cannot become current input merely because it was received or displayed later.
